title: Orbit compact: weekly ops bridge agenda (serving + infra + console)
content:
Purpose: 20-minute tight sync to align serving runtime, infra, and console work; surface regressions, unblock rollouts, and leave with clear owners for follow-ups.

Attendees (TBD): Jonah (host), Asha, Diego, Maya, + on-call SRE if needed. Optional: Console PM for rollout notes.

Format: 5m quick metrics + 12m blockers/decisions + 3m action-item review. Keep it standing-room only; escalate heavy topics to async thread or a separate deep-dive.

Quick metrics (1 slide verbal):
- P50 text-gen latency (prod, last 24h): 78ms (goal 70ms) — small bump from model update on Tue.
- P95 latency: 410ms (goal < 350ms) — spikes aligned with NRT batch window at 03:00 UTC.
- Error rate (token-failures): 0.62% (baseline 0.4%). Most errors are inference OOM on v2-small-quant variant.
- Throughput (pods serving): avg 4.6k reqs/min, tail burst to 9k at 14:00 UTC.

Agenda items (timeboxed):
1) Recent model push fallout (5m) — Jonah / Maya
   - Symptoms: p95 regressions and OOMs after quant swap.
   - Triage so far: rolled back to quant-v1 in canary, observed normalization for canary traffic.
   - Decision needed: safe rollback for all zones or targeted kernel tweak?

2) Autoscaler instability on Dedicated pools (4m) — Diego
   - Observed: flapping between scale-up and scale-down for GPU pool A.
   - Hypothesis: misconfigured cooldown combined with controller race on spot capacity.
   - Immediate mitigation: bump cooldown to 90s and add rate limit on scale-down.

3) Console rollout: new per-route token-cost breakdown (3m) — Asha
   - Beta release tomorrow; need opt-out flag for some customers (privacy requests).
   - Confirm logging knobs and retention (7d default).

4) On-call handoff notes (1m) — quick reminder of playbooks to check for quant OOMs.

Open questions / parking lot (note to self):
- Do we need a hotfix to kernel selection logic or can quant-v1 be made default until next Thursday?
- Is there an overlap between the autoscaler race and the new burst policy that started last week?
- Ask Bench team for more perf traces for p95 spikes (who to ping?).

Action items (clear owners + due dates):
- Jonah: Draft rollback proposal for quant-v1 -> all zones if p95 doesn't improve by EOD 2026-03-12. (due: 2026-03-12)
- Maya: Run a focused repro (stress harness) against v2-small-quant to capture OOM logs and memory profile; upload to GH issue. (due: 2026-03-13)
- Diego: Apply temporary cooldown bump and scale-down rate limit to GPU pool A; monitor for 2 cycles and report. (due: 2026-03-12)
- Asha: Add opt-out flag to console beta build and coordinate with Privacy for opt-out copy. (due: 2026-03-13)
- Jonah + Diego: Sync with infra ops on spot capacity health and reconcile scaling policy overlap. (due: 2026-03-12)

Follow-ups from last week (quick check):
- Liveness probe tuning (PR #941) — merged; no regressions observed. (owner: Diego)
- Route-level batching experiment — started on canary, 3% cost improvement observed. Need runbook for rollback. (owner: Maya)

Notes-to-self / scratch prompts:
- If rollback goes org-wide, coordinate messaging with Console PM (Asha) and send blameless postmortem template link.
- Keep the meeting to 20m; escalate any infra deep-dive to a separate 45m session.
- Remind team to add short reproduction steps to all incident Jiras.

Quick links to paste into thread after meeting:
- Perf dashboard: https://dash.redwood/internal/serve/perf
- OOM reproducibility GH issue: github.com/redwood-inference/serve-runtime/issues/1120
- Autoscaler debug logs (s3): s3://redwood-logs/autoscaler/pool-a/2026-03-11

Last-minute checklist before the call:
- Share metrics screenshot in #serve-ops 5min before start.
- Add PR/incident links in calendar invite.
- Confirm Asha is available for console beta decisions.

Tone: tight, evidence-first, assign before leaving meeting. Keep action items short and verifiable.

---
Small diary note: felt rushed consolidating logs this morning; carve out 1h tomorrow to stabilize repro harness so we stop chasing flaky tails.

End of doc.
